review_text_raw:
Short but unique and polished experience well worth the price.

It plays a bit more like a visual novel than a detective puzzle game in that it focuses a lot more on story than it does on detective mechanics, which is maybe a bit of a shame given how the detective puzzles are really good but somewhat underused while the story is okay but not necessarily great. Still, it manages to weave the detective and story elements really well and the whole resulting package including visual style, voice acting, and music is really good.

Overall, I adored this game.  I struggle with this next phrase because i don't fully mean it and understand why it is the way it is... but I'm glad I bought it on sale and not full price as it's not quite worth the full price.  I mostly say this due to game length and lack of choice in endings.  I took a look and it looks like this might be a first time game from this dev, who I'm guessing is solo or very small which is VERY exciting to see if this is their freshman showing.

Things I LOVED:
-Dynamic story telling.  There was a clear storyline running through from start to finish.  Not overly convoluted, not too cliche or simple.  Were the twists a little predictable?  Maybe a few.  But that didn't take away from the impact when they hit anyway.  The pacing of those drops were excellently done.
-Style was lovely.  I REALLY dug the overall look of the game.  The various tools you got to us, the puzzles you go to solve... all from a single terminal.  It made me think of a hacking game from the early 00s of gaming sites that I loved to play over and over.
-The voice acting was excellent.  Really stellar work.
-The game itself.  It's just really enjoyable.  It was well paced, the mystery was fun, the story was easy to follow, the puzzles were a bit easy but a few had some real challenges in there.  One puzzle was a bit too much of a lateral thinking puzzle, BUT that was one of the best twists of the whole game so I can overlook it. 

Things I wish were different (not bad, just things I wanted more of):
-it's far too short.  It took me about 4 hours to complete and that was going very slow and taking my time, looking at my phone a lot and doing a few other things at the same time. (thanks ADHD)  The story telling and plot that the game is driving could easily have been a full scale game.  And I'd pay good money for it, too.  This is top notch story telling from a new dev and I hope we see more.
-Lack of use of cool tools.  You're introduced to several cool mini puzzles throughout the game like a car analyzer, a bomb diffuser, and chemical component analyzer.  All of them have robust rules and options with them.  And they're all used only once.  You gave us so many cool toys.. let us play with them!!
-No story diversity with a [spoiler] really weak and bad ending [/spoiler].  While the story they have given is lovely, your choices don't matter.  There is just that ending.  I wanted more options, i wanted to affect the story with how i played and wanted the game reward cleverness (i.e. if you found a certain name on a certain list before you were told to.)

All that being said, if you like mystery games, if you like hack style games, this is a great choice.  I am very excited to see what this dev does in the future.  If this is their first showing, we are in for some real gems in the future!!

review_text_raw:
I would prefer to give this game a 5/10, but unfortunately, that's not possible on Steam, so I’m rating it negatively for interested buyers to see.

I bought the game to unravel mysteries as an FBI operative—a game I could play for several hours. The gameplay mechanics are exactly what I was hoping for, but unfortunately, some of them are only used once throughout the entire game.
The story is extremely short, with a plot that becomes obvious within the first 40 minutes of gameplay. Seriously, 2 hours of gameplay for 14€? Not to meantion an "Original Soundtrack" for another 10€. If players could skip some dialogues and cutscenes, the game would only last 30 minutes. The story feels more like a detective TV show where everything is "weird," "doesn't make sense," and "everything is interconnected."

In summary:
+ The game mechanics are awesome! - Unfortunately, their potential is wasted on a simplistic story with a soap-opera-like plot seen more than thousands of times on TV.
+ The soundtrack (not bought), sound effects, and voice acting are excellent.
- The story is simple and feels rather sloppy (95% of the ideas went into coding and mechanics, 5% into the story). Perhaps it's due to the potential for a speedrunning community?
- When I calculate the "price per hour" of the main story, this game is undoubtedly the worst in my entire game library (7€ per hour (almost 12€ if you buy the "original soundtrack"), including cutscenes and dialogues).
- The game has unskippable cutscenes (returning home), dialogues (the tutorial), and end credits, likely so that you can’t get a refund within the 2-hour Steam policy.
? If the sequel to this game will also be only 2 hours long, the developers might as well not even bother. It’s not worth the money.

If the game was a bit longer (at least 4 hours of a decent story), I would recommend it, but unfortunately, I can't.
Definitely buy it during a sale, just not now.

I'm [i]really[/i] glad to have a game like this where the story isn't just "surveillance bad".

The mechanics are good though sometimes it can be hard to scan things even when you know what to scan. Special ways to solve problems are generally only used once and can be decently complex and fun because of that. They're usually a refreshing change and can be [i]incredibly[/i] intense. I just wish certain things would be randomized between attempts.

Now for the story. Like I said, I'm very glad it didn't go for the usual story this type of game attracts. It's a fairly decent plot with likeable, well voiceacted characters and let's you figure out certain things early without being utterly obvious.

The problem is the ending. The rest will be in spoilers, though I'm not gonna say anything specific. This is basically just for people that are really adverse to any kind spoiler, no matter how small.

[spoiler]The story is very good at making you think that your choices matter; though they ultimate do not. The stakes feel astronomical in multiple situations, but turn out to be utterly meaningless in the end. And there's no easy way to say this, but:

The ending sucks. Ruining the rest of the game levels of bad.

For starters, there is only one, even if it might seem you'd have at least 2 paths to go down. On top of that it is abrupt, doesn't make any sense and the person responsible for said ending was probably meant to seem really intimidating and constantly in control. This is not the case and the person ends up looking incredibly incompetent and only seems to succeed because everyone else is even more of an idiot.

I can not overstate enough that the entire game was fun - only for the entire mood to be ruined at the end, seemingly just to set up a sequel that could've easily focused on a different conspiracy. I genuinely do not know how it was fumbled this badly.[/spoiler]

The Operator feels more like a short demo than a full game. The entire experience is over in just a few hours, making it hard to justify the full price—definitely one to buy only at a discount.

The game revolves around solving a single case from start to finish. While that might sound intriguing, it quickly becomes clear that they could have added a few standalone missions beforehand to build up engagement. Instead, you’re thrown into one investigation with no variety.

The tools available for solving the case are extremely limited. Some mechanics feel underdeveloped, and many tools are used only once, making them feel pointless rather than integral to the gameplay.

Overall, The Operator is a bland and forgettable experience. It lacks depth, variety, and replay value, making it hard to recommend.

Ending is terrible, like actually, I feel like beating the devs right now. Everything else is beautiful. Game and ending are a contrast like life and death. Played through the whole thing in one sitting. A few of the puzzles could have been reused a few more times. Things such as the car lookup software, which sound extremely important, are only used once. And I want to defuse more bombs.

Ok, now the main thing that got me really angry. Spoilers ahead, if you want to experience the story for yourself, stop reading.



You are Evan Tanner, an FBI Operator, assisting field agents by searching through files and coordinating stuff. Your first case is a murder where a man named Jenkins was shot, and a list with a bunch of names is found. The weird thing: one of the names was censored, but only after the document got secured as evidence, so theres some shady cover-up shit happening inside of the FBI.
Then, you get contacted by HAL (Alice Truman), a wanted hacker, who needs your help with uncovering said shady shit. Later, Jenkins killer gets shot by a mysterious bold man who is in no database.

A bunch of shit happens, and you find out about a biomedical company named BioM, lead by Jenkins, whose target it is to create a drug that can erase memories. Jenkins intention is to make it possible to erase trauma from peoples memories (his daughter (probably) took her life because she got traumatized or something idk and then his wife killed herself as well...). However, the funding comes from some shadow-world-government people who intend to use the drug to erase peoples minds and rewrite their memories. Spoiler: You are one of those. You are a double agent, sent to win HALs trust. But you don't know that, since your objective is deeply burried inside of your mind.
In the end, you and HAL (and some others) try to find out who the double-agent in the FBI is by infiltrating the server room. However, the hitman from earlier, who got caught at some point in the story (irrelevant) is freed by said double-agent and shoots some people. You try to escapa but get shot. Everything is covered up as you being the double-agent (which si partially true because you ARE one, but not THE one) and all your friends get shot or jailed. HAL, who gives you her identity, is compromised since you ,remeber, are a double agent, so you somehow redirect that information to the hitman guy or the shadow government or idk who the fuck but basically it was all a huge trap to infiltrate the possible resistance that could pose a threat to said shadow government. You and all your friends die and all of your actions were meaningless. THE END.

10/10 gameplay, 8/10 story, 0/10 ending

Not worth it or I had too many expectations (and a slightly exaggerated game description on the store page)

review_text_raw:
To the question of whether I'd recommend this game: it depends, but probably not. 

Full disclosure up-front: I knew nothing about this game, nor had I done any investigating as to what the game was ultimately meant to be, so my reactions here are likely influenced by it not being quite what I expected or really wanted. 

The Operator is a ultimately a fairly short, story-based narrative dressed in the clothing of a detective game, rather than a detective game where you work through puzzles and solve mysteries. 

The game's mechanics and design were an interesting approach to storytelling, but felt quite underused, which probably goes more to my expectations of wanting a detective puzzle game with a greater variety in cases to solve. In most instances a new mechanic was introduced for one section, only for it to never be used again. 

The story itself is passable. I've consumed my fair share of content in the thriller, detective, mystery and conspiracy genres, and nothing here felt fresh to me in terms of the plot; you could see where the story was going from a mile away and the ultimate outcomes fairly early on. 

If you want a mystery story with conspiracy elements woven in, then this is probably worth a go. If that's not what you're in the market for, then you can probably give this a miss.

review_text_raw:
The Operator is a really fun, if unbearably short, adventure game that scratches the itch I've had since playing Hypnospace Outlaw. Cyber-sleuthing to solve and aid crimes and slowly diving into a conspiracy? What's not to like?

I wish it was a bit longer or the main plot was a bit drawn out, however. The game starts you off with a simple tutorial, but it drops you immediately into a fullfledged conspiracy that's the driving force of the entire game. Some little bit of fluff would have been nice. Analyze a video to solve an armed robbery, cross-reference tattoos to uncover gang affiliations, find out a victim's next of kin to get more information, or even just zoom in an ID what home a missing cat belongs to. There's endless possibilities for this kind of concept that are just underutilized. It left me wanting more when the reality was I only had a limited set of things to do.

The game is still exceptionally well made and the soundtrack keeps you engaged through all the twists and reveals, even if they were obvious in the first place. It's a good afternoon game.

I've been really into narrative puzzle games lately and was excited to give this one a shot. The gameplay and interface are really tight and the story is interesting. However, in terms of a puzzle game it never feels like it ramps up. The story is broken up into such small pieces that there's no real need to sift through different possibilities. Every step towards solution seems pretty obvious. There are fun mechanics introduced and then only used once. You're never really challenged to combine the skills or info you have gathered over the course of the game. In the end it feels like a kind of short visual narrative with a fun interface. If they made another one focused on more difficult scenarios and a wider scope I would probably try it.

Also, nobody had cell phones or digital cameras in 1992/3. Not sure why they chose to set the game in that particular time period, it makes a lot of the technology feel very out of place.

The game has a great concept and some thrilling moments. The developers did a fantastic job immersing you in the feeling of being a "cog in a machine". The music, interface design, story theme, and execution were excellent. I especially enjoyed the quiet moments where I could read through various documents and explore the backstory and world the developers created.

That’s why it pains me so much that all this hard work feels utterly underutilized. You’re essentially handheld and dragged through a linear story, with little to no impact from your choices. There are intricate mechanics that seem fun once you struggle through their first use, but they are never used again. It is just a little bit more "game" than a "interactive movie".

I don’t want to be cruel—I can see the developers put a lot of effort into it—but it was just far too short.

review_text_raw:
Maybe my expectations weren't set properly but I was going into this game hoping to fill the shoes of an FBI operator : 

- Analyse photos, videos, samples
- Search and match data accross differents sources
- Analyse piles of documents or suspects conversations
- etc.

in order to make some deductions and help ongoing investigations. 

This is what you get for the first 25% of the game. 
After that, it slowly shifts into a narrative driven experience, where your choices don't matter (the game is programmed to end one way), the scenario is at best foreseeable at worst blatantly cliché. All the investigation mechanics that you were taught are thrown out the window and never used again. 

The scenario felt like drinking room-temperature water. It's uninteresting, not particulary pleasant and completely forgettable. Overall it feels like a huge bait and switch

review_text_raw:
Quite different from anything I've played.

The story is engaging and the mystery unfolds in a very interesting way. Unfortunately, the gameplay leaves a bit to be desired.

With the exception of HumanDB, most of the tools in the terminal are only used once, and you have few opportunities to use them to solve puzzles outside of what the game wants you to do, since most of them only have one solution.

The game could also use a chapter selection, since, to get certain achievements, you would need to play the entire game again.

Other than that, it's a fun game that doesn't overstay its welcome and leaves you wanting more. Hope they make a sequel

[b]7.5/10[/b]

I'm simply impressed. It's not what I expected, but in a good way. I expected it to be a game where you "just" solve cases as an "FDI" (FBI) Operative. I didn't expect it to have such a great story/plot.

The devs should add a "Freeplay" mode though where you just investigate and solve cases without this crazy big plot behind it because currently some of the features are really underutilized because you literally only use them a single time in the story, which is a bummer because they are really fun to use. This mode and the cases could even come as a DLC to pay off the costs of making the cases.

review_text_raw:
The Operator has some nice computer monitor and app effects, and the core mechanics are fun while they last. However, many visual elements do not quite match up: the photos look realistic, but the CCTV feeds often feel like old 3D graphics, which breaks immersion.

I enjoyed the investigative gameplay, but the game is very short, and most mechanics are only used once. I would have preferred a more grounded, realistic story instead of a conspiracy that unfolds over three days.

Overall, I enjoyed my time with it, but I do not think I will ever replay it.

Had a blast playing this game! It’s fun and engaging, though there are a few minor bugs.

However, there are a few downsides. Some mechanics or features are only used once throughout the entire game, which feels like a missed opportunity. Additionally, certain cutscenes are unskippable—fine for the first playthrough, but frustrating when you want to explore different paths. Speaking of different paths, the story can feel a bit restrictive. While there are some choices to make, they often lead to the same outcome, limiting the sense of true player agency.
